punchline: McDonald's took the beef fat out of its fries in 1990 and then had to add beef flavour back into the oil.
thirty_sec: For years McDonald's fries were cooked mostly in beef fat. Phil Sokolof ran full-page newspaper ads attacking the chain over fat, and in summer 1990 McDonald's announced a move to vegetable oil. The fat had also supplied the taste, so a flavouring was added to bring it back. Published accounts say the flavouring contains no actual beef but is made from wheat and milk derivatives.
